purpose.text: Use the configured Google Analytics 4 property and Search Console site to answer traffic, content, audience, engagement, conversion, revenue, realtime, and search performance questions; compare periods and look up metrics for selected pages; discover available GA4 fields; and, when the selected operation calls for it, inspect a URL or submit an indexing notification. Preserve analysis results and turn saved data into a readable summary through the documented workflow.

evidences.reason: Identifies the toolkit and the user goals it is designed to serve.
Defines analysis, persistence, and summarization as successive phases.
Distinguishes the GA4, Search Console, indexing, and field discovery operations.
Distinguishes URL inspection from submitting recrawl and removal notifications.
Specifies a targeted GA4 lookup for selected page paths.

requirements.text: For toolkit setup, install the script dependencies from the scripts directory using npm and use Node.js 18 or newer.

evidences.reason: Specifies the dependency installation command and directory.
The setup script installs dependencies from its own directory.

requirements.text: For the full toolkit setup, use a Google Cloud project with the Analytics Data, Search Console, and Indexing APIs enabled and a service account with access to the intended GA4 property and Search Console site. Configure the property ID, service account email and private key, and Search Console site URL through the documented environment settings. The file based setup places .env in the project root, and the loader reads from the working directory.

evidences.reason: Names the environment settings, file location, and Google project and account prerequisites.
Shows where the environment file is loaded.
Identifies the runtime settings and supports escaped newlines in the private key.

requirements.text: When initializing any of the three authenticated clients, validate that GA4_PROPERTY_ID, GA4_CLIENT_EMAIL, and GA4_PRIVATE_KEY are present and report missing settings as errors. Use the configured service account email and private key for authentication, interpreting escaped newlines in the key as line breaks.

evidences.reason: Defines the settings read from the environment and the private key normalization.
Explicitly defines the three required settings and the resulting validation errors.
The GA4 client validates settings before using the service account credentials.
Shows the service account authentication and the validation gate for the Search Console client.
The Indexing client applies the same validation before initialization.

requirements.text: Address GA4 reports, realtime data, and metadata to the configured GA4 property. Address Search Console analytics and URL inspection to the configured Search Console site, and inspect the specified URL within that site. Indexing notifications address the specified URL.

evidences.reason: Defines the GA4 property resource using the configured ID.
Targets the configured property in standard reports.
Targets the configured property in realtime reporting.
Targets the configured property's metadata resource.
Uses the configured site for search analytics.
Addresses the update notification to the requested URL.
The inspection request separately identifies the inspection URL and the configured site.

requirements.text: For operations that accept a historical date range, honor the selected endpoints. Accept days-to-today shorthand and explicit start and end dates; GA4 date range objects may also use GA4 relative endpoints. Search Console uses calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD form, including when converting shorthand. Use GA4_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE when a range is omitted, with 30d as the built-in default. The parsers fall back to 30 days when a string is not recognized as shorthand.

evidences.reason: Documents the supported date forms and configurable default.
Defines the built-in setting when no default is configured.
Preserves supplied endpoint objects, parses shorthand, and defines the GA4 fallback.
Requires calendar dates for Search Console and defines shorthand conversion and fallback.

requirements.text: For a custom GA4 report, use the requested dimension and metric lists and the applicable date range, and return structured report rows with the corresponding dimension and metric values.

evidences.reason: Defines the required dimension and metric lists, optional date range, and report result.
Defines the structured report response.
Shows how the selected fields and dates define the report.

requirements.text: When provided for a custom GA4 report, honor the requested dimension filters, sort order, and row limit. These controls are optional and have no documented default values.

evidences.reason: Documents the three optional controls and their purposes.
Declares the controls in the report options.

evidences.reason: Specifies the page view dimensions and metrics.

evidences.reason: Specifies the source, medium, and campaign dimensions and the traffic metrics.

evidences.reason: Defines the audience breakdown and its metrics.

evidences.reason: Defines the event grouping and measures.

requirements.text: For the standard conversion report, group by eventName and sessionSource and report conversions and totalRevenue.

evidences.reason: Defines the conversion report's event and source grouping and measures.

requirements.text: For the standard e-commerce report, report totalRevenue, ecommercePurchases, and averagePurchaseRevenue by date and transactionId.

evidences.reason: Specifies the four components of the comprehensive site snapshot.

evidences.reason: Defines the three complementary views for the traffic deep dive.

evidences.reason: Requires page views, landing pages, and exit pages in the content analysis.

requirements.text: Compare exactly two supplied date ranges using the same dimension and metric selection for both. Default to the date dimension and the activeUsers, sessions, and screenPageViews metrics. Present the results side by side in the supplied period order and keep each result associated with its original range.

evidences.reason: Defines the comparison as side-by-side results for two ranges.
Defines both range inputs, shared field defaults, and the association of each original range with its result.

evidences.reason: Specifies the three components of the snapshot.

requirements.text: For bulk GA4 lookup, treat the supplied strings as page paths. Trim whitespace, add a leading slash where missing, and preserve existing trailing slashes. Match the normalized paths with a case-insensitive pagePath inclusion filter. Return no filter for an empty path list and return an empty report with zero rows without issuing a GA4 report for that list.

evidences.reason: Defines the path normalization and dimension filter helpers.
Specifies trailing slash preservation, the empty filter case, and case-insensitive matching.
Handles the empty list before accessing the GA4 client.

requirements.text: For a nonempty bulk lookup, report metrics for the specified page paths using pagePath and pageTitle as dimensions and the selected date range. Use the selected metrics if supplied; otherwise use screenPageViews, activeUsers, averageSessionDuration, bounceRate, and engagementRate.

evidences.reason: Defines the targeted lookup, date and metric options, and default metric set.
Specifies the grouping dimensions and applies the selected metrics and path filter.

requirements.text: For a single recrawl request, submit a URL_UPDATED notification for the supplied full URL. Return the notification URL, update type, and notification time. Use the submitted URL and current time as fallbacks when the corresponding notification values are absent. Treat the result as notification submission rather than confirmation of indexing.

evidences.reason: Requires a full URL and identifies the update notification and returned fields.
Shows the notification action, the source of the returned URL and time, and their fallbacks.

requirements.text: For an explicit removal request, submit a URL_DELETED notification for the supplied URL. Return the notification URL, deletion type, and notification time, using the submitted URL and current time as fallbacks if those notification values are absent.

evidences.reason: Defines removal as a distinct action with a deletion notification result.
Specifies the deletion notification and the fallback URL and time.

requirements.text: For the low level batch recrawl operation, submit notifications sequentially in the supplied URL order to avoid rate limiting. Return the corresponding notification results in that order on successful completion.

evidences.reason: Requires sequential processing and an array of notification results.
Processes the supplied URLs one at a time and appends each corresponding result.

requirements.text: For the high level reindexing operation, process the supplied URLs sequentially and report a submission or failure for each item in input order. Include the notification result on submission and the original URL and error on failure. Continue with later URLs after a per-URL failure.

evidences.reason: Identifies reindexing as a multi-URL operation distinct from checking status.
Defines per-item submission and failure results, catches errors inside the loop, and returns the aggregate.

requirements.text: For detailed URL inspection, report the inspected URL's index verdict and coverage state and include available crawl, indexing, canonical, mobile usability, and rich result details and the inspection link when returned. When the index verdict or coverage state is unavailable, report NEUTRAL or Unknown respectively.

evidences.reason: Defines the detailed inspection purpose and result.
Defines the core and optional inspection fields.
Defines the index status fallbacks and conditional sections.

requirements.text: For a high level status check, inspect each supplied URL and return its original URL, indexed flag, and corresponding index status in input order. evidences.reason: Identifies the multi-URL status check as a separate operation.
Defines the indexed test, the per-item projection and identity, and the error handling.

issues.reason: Apply date ranges to operations that document a historical range, and apply the date format appropriate to the service. The general wording does not extend historical dates to realtime or indexing operations.

evidences.reason: The high level SEO page analysis describes its pages as ranked by clicks.
The standalone top-pages reference ranks them by search impressions.
The overview uses the same top-pages helper.
The SEO analysis uses that helper while describing the selection as ranked by clicks.
The direct-run help also describes the standalone helper as ranking pages by clicks.

issues.reason: Clicks and impressions can produce different top-page sets. Preserve the detailed standalone contract and the high level clicks description at their stated scopes. The shared call and conflicting standalone help do not establish a single ranking or show how the scopes obtain different rankings.

evidences.reason: Describes a device breakdown with queries without stating its row granularity.
Describes a breakdown for queries but obtains query and device results separately.
The query helper groups only by query.
The device helper groups only by device.

issues.reason: A device breakdown for each query would require query-by-device information. A separate device view alongside the top queries can be produced with device totals alone. Both readings are supported by the source package, so the task retains the two views without asserting a joint grouping.

This can change which result is returned. Preserve the operation restriction without treating prefix collisions as a documented requirement.

Encourages requesting summaries after data collection.
